contract: design(problem) -> (materials, thicknesses): a list of 'L'/'H' labels and a list of physical thicknesses in nm, layers ordered from the air side to the substrate. problem gives ambient_index 1.0, substrate_index 1.52, materials {'L': 1.38, 'H': 2.35} (lossless, non-dispersive), band_nm [400, 800], max_layers 20, max_total_nm 1000 and max_layer_nm 400; every thickness must lie in [0, max_layer_nm] and the sum must not exceed max_total_nm. design runs in a sandboxed subprocess with a 60 s CPU budget. Score (minimize): mean normal-incidence reflectance in percent over 401 equally spaced wavelengths in the band, computed exactly with the characteristic-matrix method (bare glass: 4.26 %)
notes: The thin-film model is exact for homogeneous lossless layers at normal incidence; real coatings add dispersion, absorption, interface roughness and thickness errors, which are not modelled. The materials, band and limits are a local choice in the spirit of the single-band antireflection studies of Dobrowolski et al. (1996); no published value exists for this exact specification.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Physics: broadband antireflection coating design
description: Design a stack of at most twenty low- and high-index layers (1.38 and 2.35) on glass that minimizes the mean reflectance between 400 and 800 nm at normal incidence, with at most 1000 nm of total coating. The evaluator checks the constraints and computes the reflectance spectrum exactly with the thin-film characteristic-matrix method.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Dobrowolski, Tikhonravov, Trubetskov, Sullivan and Verly (1996), Optimal single-band normal-incidence antireflection coatings: how the lowest attainable average reflectance depends on bandwidth, index contrast and total optical thickness.
Tikhonravov, Trubetskov and DeBell (1996), Application of the needle optimization technique to the design of optical coatings: the standard numerical method for this design problem.

limitations: Layers are lossless and non-dispersive with fixed indices, and only normal incidence is scored; real coatings need dispersion data, absorption, oblique incidence and tolerance to thickness errors.

The specification (two materials, 400-800 nm, 20 layers, 1000 nm) is a local choice in the spirit of Dobrowolski et al. (1996); no published optimum exists for it, so scores compare designs under this model only.
The mean is taken over 401 equally spaced wavelengths, so a design could in principle exploit the sampling between grid points; the reported maximum reflectance helps to spot that.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value for this exact specification. For context, bare glass reflects 4.26 %, the single quarter-wave seed gives 1.58 %, and a multistart local optimization of alternating 14-layer stacks run during task construction reached 0.084 %.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Design a multilayer thin-film stack that minimizes the average reflectance of a glass surface over the visible band.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Antireflection coatings are needed on essentially every optical surface, and how low the average reflectance can go for a given number of layers, index contrast and total thickness is a long-studied design question with published limits.
